topic: Implicit Differentiation: Unlocking the Slopes of Complex Curves
target_audience: University Freshmen and Advanced High School Calculus Students

sections.title: The Great Divide: Explicit vs. Implicit
sections.content: Introduce the difference between explicit functions (y is isolated) and implicit equations (x and y are tangled). Use a visual of a 'solved' puzzle vs. a 'jumbled' puzzle. Explain that while we can't always solve for y, we can still find the rate of change.
sections.example: Explicit: y = x² (A simple path). Implicit: x² + y² = 25 (A circular racetrack where x and y are inseparable partners).

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Chain Rule Reminder
sections.content: Review the Chain Rule as the 'Golden Key'. Emphasize that whenever we differentiate a term containing 'y' with respect to 'x', we must treat 'y' as an inner function [y(x)]. Graphically show a 'function within a function' as a set of nested Russian dolls.
sections.example: To differentiate y³, think of it as [f(x)]³. The derivative is 3y² multiplied by the 'hidden' derivative dy/dx.

sections.title: The Step-by-Step Algorithm
sections.content: Outline the three-step process: 1. Differentiate both sides with respect to x. 2. Apply the Chain Rule to all 'y' terms (tagging them with dy/dx). 3. Use algebra to isolate dy/dx on one side. Use an animation of a balance scale to show operations happening to both sides simultaneously.
sections.example: Visualizing 'dy/dx' as a specific colored 'sticky note' that gets attached to every term where y was differentiated.

sections.title: Guided Practice: The Circular Track
sections.content: Apply the steps to the equation of a circle x² + y² = 25. Show the transformation from an equation of position to an equation of slope. Use a character like 'Dash the Cheetah' running along the circle to represent a point (x, y).
sections.example: At point (3, 4) on the circle, we calculate dy/dx = -x/y. Plugging in the numbers, the cheetah's instantaneous direction (slope) is -3/4.

sections.title: Complex Curves: The Folium of Descartes
sections.content: Demonstrate the power of the technique on a 'looping' curve where solving for y is nearly impossible. Use a 3D-style animation to show how the tangent line 'glides' smoothly around the loop, even when the curve doubles back on itself.
sections.example: Equation: x³ + y³ = 6xy. Show how the Product Rule must be used on the right side (6x * y) to correctly find the slope of this 'looped' knot.

sections.title: Summary and Geometric Insight
sections.content: Recap the core concept: Implicit differentiation allows us to find the slope (dy/dx) at any point on a curve without needing a clean 'y =' formula. End with a visual montage of various implicit shapes (ellipses, hyperbolas, and hearts) with their tangent lines flashing.
sections.example: A 'Heart Curve' (x² + y² - 1)³ - x²y³ = 0. Even for love, calculus can find the exact slope of the curve at any moment!
